item.title: Trains collide in Egypt, killing at least 7 and injuring more than 100
item.description:
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital of Cairo, killing at least seven people and injuring more than 100 others, authorities said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 32 miles south of Cairo, when a train traveling to the southwestern Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the Transportation Ministry. One of the trains derailed, it said, but did not specify which.
People stand at the site of a train collision in al-Ayyat in Giza province, Egypt, on Nov. 8, 2026.
AFP via Getty Images
The Health Ministry said at least four people were killed and 88 others were wounded. The injured were taken to nearby hospitals for treatment, it said.
A train driver was among those killed in the collision, the Health Ministry said.
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Nov. 8, derailing several carriages, killing four and injuring dozens, according to the authorities.
AFP via Getty Images
President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi said in a social media post he is following the aftermath of the train collision "with great concern and extend my deepest condolences to the families of those who lost their lives."
"I have directed state agencies to provide the necessary medical care, promptly investigate the circumstances of the accident and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent," he wrote.

item.title: Transcript: Rep.-elect Nancy Lacore on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Nov. 8, 2026
item.description:
The following is the full transcript of the interview with Rep.-elect Nancy Lacore, a portion of which aired on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" on Nov. 8, 2026.
MARGARET BRENNAN: We go now to Retired Vice Admiral and Congresswoman-Elect Nancy Lacore, a Democrat in South Carolina. Good morning to you.
REPRESENTATIVE-ELECT NANCY LACORE (SC-01): Good morning.
MARGARET BRENNAN: So, you flipped a seat that Republicans have held for 43 of the last 45 years, and you won by just about 3,000 votes. What is the message that you are taking to Washington from your voters?
REP.-ELECT LACORE: Well, we knew this was going to be a hard race to win, and we knew it was going to take really reaching past the Democratic Party into the Independents and moderate Republicans. And that was our focus early on. It started with getting an endorsement from a Republican mayor here in Mount Pleasant, which is the largest municipality in the district. And that sort of set us on that path to start building that very broad coalition that we knew would win. And I really think my background of 35 years nonpartisan military leadership is one that really helped bring voters over from those other parties and make sure that we had the- the votes that we needed to win this district.
MARGARET BRENNAN: Well, I understand you were a registered Republican until 2016, and you said that you had left the party because of Donald Trump. He's the president you will have to work with to get things done in the next two years. What opportunities do you see?
REP.-ELECT LACORE: I see a lot of opportunities because of what the new Congress is going to look like. You know, there's a significant majority this time. There are a lot of veterans who are now, you know, elected, you know, soon to be official congressmen and women. And as veterans, we don't really care what your political affiliation is. We just focus on achieving the mission. And I think that's what you're going to see out of this new Congress.

item.title: Iran downplays new U.S. task force aimed at disrupting land routes
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: Central Command also announced the creation of Task Force Iron Gate, which is supposed to extend the success of the naval blockade to overland routes of trade. The group will be tasked with preventing military technology and illegal revenue streams from entering or exiting Iranian borders, including via the Caspian Sea, but it was unclear if any military force would be brought to bear. Iran's military on Sunday dismissed the new task force as "word play."The U.S. military's Central Command announced Friday it is offering up to $20 million and possible relocation in exchange for information about Iran's nuclear program, its facilities, equipment or personnel.President Trump confirmed on Friday the U.S. carried out "minor strikes" on Iran, after local state media reported missiles striking Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz

item.title: Poland mourns Krakow shooting victims as terrorism probe launched
item.description:
Poland began two days of national mourning on Sunday, a day after a 24-year-old man with far-right views opened fire in a busy central square in Krakow, killing six people and wounding 15 others.
The attack, which Poland's defense minister described as an "act of terror," happened in Main Square, a major tourist hub in the heart of Krakow's Old Town.
The alleged shooter, a Polish man, was shot and wounded by police.
The prosecutors said on Sunday they started an investigation for murder and attempted murder of numerous people, including police officers, with the act "constituting a terrorist offense."
Police officers work next to Krakow's Main Market a day after a gunman opened fire, killing six people and wounding around a dozen others in the historic center of Poland's city of Krakow on Nov. 8, 2026.
Wojtek RADWANSKI /AFP via Getty Images
Four women and two men were killed in the Main Square shooting. Three of the women and one of the men were Polish, Krzysztof Jan Klęczar, the Malopolska regional governor, said on Sunday. A man from the U.K. and a woman from an unidentified foreign country were also among the dead.
The bodies of three people — the assailant's sister, mother and father — were found at the man's house in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city about 93 miles northeast of Krakow. They likely died from gunshot wounds, authorities said.
Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the suspect holds "very radical" and "ultranationalistic" views.
"Everything indicates that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies," Kierwiński said at a news conference.

item.title: Villa Vie Odyssey "forever cruise" residents want their ship back
item.description:
As the Villa Vie Odyssey cruise ship makes its way from Cambodia to Singapore, where it could potentially be auctioned off by its lender, CBS News has learned of at least two resident-led efforts to reclaim the vessel.
One effort recently failed after a lender denied funding to residents of the luxury "forever cruise." However, a second effort to buy the ship is still very much active, according to two sources familiar with the matter. It is led by another group hoping to buy the ship at auction, the sources said.
The second effort would not involve Villa Vie Residences' founder and executive chairman Mike Petterson, according to sources involved in the discussions.
Petterson said he believed he had an operational partner to rescue the ship, but that did not pan out, which led to the ship being taken by its lender.
Now, Petterson says he believes he could still get the ship back and is continuing to look for potential investors to take over the ship for good. Another option would be to raise the funds to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and sell the company. He no longer wants to be involved in company leadership.
"I'm not going to be the front face person of a company any time soon," Petterson told CBS News.
CBS News has also learned that a group of residents is considering legal action over fuel loans that were provided to the company in April — when residents said they raised more than $2 million dollars to keep the ship afloat.
The fuel loan program promised up to a 24% return if residents invested more money to help with the rising cost of fuel.
In a copy of an agreement obtained by CBS News, which appears to be from Villa Vie, the loan is described as "Unsecured" without "Collateral or Guarantees."

item.title: More than 600,000 left with no power in Ukraine after strikes, authorities say
item.description:
Hundreds of thousands of people were left without power after Russian strikes hit Ukraine's energy infrastructure, authorities said on Sunday.
In the central Dnipropetrovsk region, "more than 600,000 residents of the region have been left without power," power company DTEK said on Telegram after a "night attack has damaged important energy facilities".
It said the company was working to restore electricity but the task was "complicated by repeated attacks".
Ukrainian President Volodymyr previously accused Russia of ramping up attacks on Ukraine ahead of trilateral talks next week with Russia.
In another strike, a Russian drone hit "a critical infrastructure facility" in the northeastern Kharkiv region, the mayor of Zlatopil city, Mykola Baksheyev, said on social media.
"Nearly 250,000 customers in the Kharkiv region were left without power," Baksheyev said.
A separate wave of attacks caused a power outage in the centre of Kyiv on November 7, 2026.
Sergei SUPINSKY /Getty Images
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the night-time strikes had triggered "widespread power outages across the country".
"In the Zhytomyr region alone, 140 apartment buildings were left without heating following a Russian strike," he said, as temperatures in Ukraine already hovered around freezing.
He also said Russia had launched a drone at Komyshuvakha, a village in the Zaporizhzhia region where Moscow had hit an aid distribution centre on Monday in one of the deadliest attacks of the war.
The death toll has risen to 55 people, Zelenskyy said. Emergency services previously put it at 50 killed.

item.title: Italy's leader blames pro-Russian hackers for personal data leaks
item.description:
Italy's prime minister blamed pro-Russian hackers for leaking the country's foreign minister's data onto the dark web.
Italian foreign minister Antonio Tajani said on Saturday he has been subjected to intimidation and that his personal data was leaked because of his support for Ukraine, but did not specify who was behind it.
In a post on X, Tajani blamed "cybercriminals" for posting his personal data on the dark web, a term used to describe a section of the internet only accessible with specialist software, commonly associated with criminal activities.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky shakes hands with Italy's Prime Minister, Giorgia Meloni during a press point at Palazzo Chigi after their meeting in Rome on April 15, 2026.
Tiziana FABI /Getty Images
In a separate statement on Saturday, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed "pro-Russian hackers" for the leaks.
Meloni expressed her "full solidarity" with the foreign minister over "what has come to light regarding the activities of pro-Russian hackers and the dissemination of personal data relating to him on the dark web."
"The sale of confidential information about institutional representatives is a cause of serious concern and must be tackled with the utmost determination," Meloni added.
Tajani said the leaks have been going for days and expose him to threats and intimidation. He added that his family have also been targeted and the perpetrators are still looking for more information.
"Our position on Ukraine is the political reason I have been targeted," the minister said. "Defending the freedom of a sovereign state, taking a clear stand in support of a nation's democracy and independence, is dangerous for these criminal entities."
